purpose: Official-source safety reference for an educational supplement-priority planner; not an individual clearance or prescription.
population: Generally healthy nonpregnant adults age 18 or older. Individual eligibility is unknown when the interface collects only priorities.

globalPolicy.referenceDisplayLabel: Adult reference option; health, medicines and current intake not checked.
referenceScenarioAssumptions: generally healthy adult age 18 or older
not pregnant, trying to conceive or breastfeeding
caffeine only in the morning and at least 8 hours before bedtime
globalPolicy.referenceScenarioAutoSelection: Creatine for Strength and a 75 mg caffeine serving for Focus may be selected within this explicitly stated hypothetical adult scenario. It is not a verified personal recommendation; unknown actual user intake remains unknown.
conservativeExclusions: pregnant, trying to conceive or breastfeeding
globalPolicy.exclusionStatus: Product abstention policy. These are not assertions that every ingredient is harmful in every listed circumstance.
globalPolicy.noEstablishedUlMeans: No recognized numeric tolerable upper limit in the cited guidance; it does not mean unlimited intake is safe.
globalPolicy.productQuality: Prefer accurately labeled single-ingredient products with independent quality testing. FDA does not approve supplements for safety and effectiveness before marketing.

ingredients.name: Creatine monohydrate

referenceDose.basis: Conservative product reference within NIH ODS typical 3-5 g/day maintenance; not a UL.

upperLimits.scope: Do not substitute study high doses for a population UL.

ingredients.doseAccounting: Count all creatine-containing products. Label the monohydrate mass consistently; do not silently interchange creatine base and monohydrate.
screening: kidney disease or kidney-risk history requires clinician review
pregnancy and breastfeeding excluded by conservative planner policy
medicines and current supplements must be reviewed
ingredients.missingInformationCopy: 3 g/day is an adult training reference. Kidney health and medicines are unverified, so this is not personal clearance.
priorityConstraints: Strength benefit presumes ongoing high-intensity or resistance training.
Do not automatically increase the dose when Focus, Calm, Memory or Energy or Strength sliders rise.
Do not claim established healthy-adult cognitive enhancement or endurance benefit from this reference dose.

ingredients.name: Caffeine

referenceDose.basis: Conservative product range, not a government recommended intake. If modeled at 25 mg per item, three together provide a 75 mg reference serving.

upperLimits.scope: All caffeine sources combined in most healthy nonpregnant adults; individual sensitivity and medications can require less.
All sources in the same occasion for the general healthy adult population.
EFSA pregnancy/lactation all-source reference; the planner excludes these populations rather than generating a dose.

ingredients.doseAccounting: Count coffee, tea, chocolate, energy drinks, pre-workout products, supplements and medicines. Unknown baseline intake prevents a checked all-source total; never assume it is zero.
screening: caffeine sensitivity or prior adverse effects

timing.basis: Conservative product rule based on NIH NHLBI guidance that caffeine effects can last up to 8 hours; no guarantee of no sleep effect.
timing.whenBedtimeUnknown: morning-reference-only; do not fabricate a personal cutoff

ingredients.missingInformationCopy: Morning-only reference. Your existing caffeine and sleep timing are unknown; the all-source total has not been checked.
priorityConstraints: Sleep can veto caffeine even if Focus is high.
When Sleep or Calm is dominant, select a nonstimulant approach or abstain instead of escalating caffeine.
Do not add melatonin or magnesium to compensate for caffeine-related sleep loss.
Never offer bulk pure caffeine powders or concentrated liquids.
Rising Focus cannot push dose beyond the product cap; ranking changes inclusion, not unlimited dose.

prototypeUnits.timing: single morning serving; at least 8 hours before bedtime

ingredients.name: Magnesium

referenceDose.frequency: only if a dietary shortfall or clinician-supported need is established
referenceDose.basis: Conservative product range; not a proven healthy-adult sleep dose.

upperLimits.scope: U.S. adults: magnesium from supplements and medications only. Naturally present food magnesium is excluded.
EU adults: readily dissociable magnesium salts and compounds such as MgO in supplements, water or added to foods; excludes magnesium naturally present in foods and beverages.

productCap.unit: mg elemental magnesium/day added by planner

ingredients.doseAccounting: Use elemental magnesium on the Supplement Facts panel, not the mass of glycinate/citrate/other compound. Include multivitamins, antacids and laxatives in the U.S. supplemental total; consider fortified sources for the EFSA scope.
adverseEffects: toxicity risk rises with impaired renal function

interactions.note: NIH ODS: antibiotics at least 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after magnesium; a pharmacist should review the actual medicine schedule.
NIH ODS: separate magnesium by at least 2 hours.
May alter magnesium status; clinician review rather than automatic replacement.

ingredients.missingInformationCopy: Not added: dietary need, kidney health and other magnesium sources are unknown.
priorityConstraints: Sleep alone does not establish magnesium need.
Do not promise better sleep or relaxation to generally healthy adults.
A below-UL reference dose cannot override kidney disease or medication screening.

ingredients.name: Vitamin D
ingredients.doseReason: Deficiency management and dose belong to clinician assessment. Priority sliders do not diagnose deficiency.

upperLimits.scope: Adults: total oral intake from foods, fortified foods and supplements. This is a limit, not a target or default deficiency-treatment dose.

ingredients.doseAccounting: 1 mcg vitamin D = 40 IU. Count multivitamins, vitamin D products, fortified food and combination calcium-vitamin D products.
adverseEffects: excess intake can cause hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria
severe toxicity can cause kidney failure and arrhythmia
interactions: thiazide diuretics plus vitamin D may increase hypercalcemia risk, especially with compromised kidney function
orlistat, steroids and some statins can alter absorption, metabolism or interaction risk
ingredients.missingInformationCopy: Not added: deficiency status, existing intake and medicines are unknown.
priorityConstraints: Do not infer deficiency from low Calm, Focus, Strength, Memory or Energy or Sleep.
Clinician-directed treatment may differ from population limits; the app should not simulate treatment.

ingredients.name: Omega-3 EPA + DHA

upperLimits.scope: The FNB has not established an omega-3 UL. FDA/EFSA findings of safety up to about 5 g/day EPA+DHA supplements are not a target dose or an established UL.

ingredients.doseAccounting: Count EPA plus DHA, not the front-label grams of fish oil. Review all products; include food for adequacy assessment.
adverseEffects: 4 g/day over years increased atrial fibrillation risk slightly in trials among people with cardiovascular disease or high risk
interactions: anticoagulants require review and monitoring; do not state all omega-3 use necessarily causes clinically significant bleeding
ingredients.missingInformationCopy: Not added: a healthy-brain benefit and personal indication are not established.
priorityConstraints: Do not auto-add for Focus or healthy-adult brain protection.
Do not use 5 g/day safety discussion as a planner dose.

ingredients.name: Melatonin
ingredients.doseReason: No universal nightly dose: timing, indication and duration matter. Consider only a specific short-term circadian indication with clinician/pharmacist guidance.

upperLimits.scope: Short-term use appears safe for most people; long-term safety remains unclear. No unlimited or blanket daily safety claim.

interactions: epilepsy or blood-thinning medicines require medical supervision
any regular medicines should be reviewed
ingredients.missingInformationCopy: Not added: sleep timing, indication, medicines and duration are unknown.
priorityConstraints: Sleep priority is not an indication for chronic daily melatonin.
No melatonin prescription for chronic insomnia; NCCIH reports insufficient evidence for that use.
Do not counterbalance stimulant use with a sedating supplement.

ingredients.name: Protein powder
ingredients.doseReason: Use only to fill an established gap between diet and an appropriate total protein target, not an automatic extra serving.

upperLimits.scope: FNB has not set a protein UL; it advises caution with high supplemental intakes because long-term adverse-effect data are limited.

referenceTargets.athleteReference: 1.2-2.0 g/kg/day total protein; not a prescription for every user

ingredients.doseAccounting: Food protein plus powders, bars, shakes and other supplements all count. Body weight, training and diet are needed to establish a shortfall.
screening: kidney disease requires individualized dietary advice
milk or soy allergy and formulation-specific allergens
pregnancy or other conditions outside planner population
ingredients.missingInformationCopy: Not added: total dietary intake and an appropriate protein target are unknown.
priorityConstraints: Strength alone does not imply a dietary shortfall.
Do not claim renal harm in healthy adults at ordinary dietary targets; the exclusion addresses known disease and missing screening.

ingredients.name: L-theanine

referenceDose.basis: Evidence-research candidate only; not an established safety UL or a universal recommended intake.

upperLimits.scope: Food GRAS notices apply to intended conditions of use; they do not establish an unrestricted daily supplement limit or efficacy.

ingredients.safetyUncertainty: FDA's 2024 compounding review found oral use generally well tolerated, but adverse-event reporting was missing in many trials and attribution was confounded in others. The review is about compounded drugs and must not be presented as a dietary-supplement ban.
ingredients.shortTermTrialSafety: FDA reviewed 19 studies in 554 healthy adults exposed to 50-600 mg/day for one day to six weeks. Six studies reported no adverse events; thirteen did not discuss adverse events. This supports a short-term tolerability context, not proven long-term daily safety.
adverseEffects: gastrointestinal or sedating effects have been reported, with uncertain attribution in the reviewed studies
screening: pregnancy and breastfeeding excluded by conservative product policy
medicines, comorbidities and existing supplement doses need review
do not assume theanine neutralizes caffeine risks
ingredients.missingInformationCopy: Not added automatically: long-term daily safety and your medicines have not been assessed.
priorityConstraints: Optional evidence candidate for acute attention, not automatic Calm, Sleep or Memory or Energy coverage.
Do not use GRAS status as proof that the planner combination or repeated dosing is safe.

interconnectedPriorityRules.rule: Eligibility and all-source exposure constraints run before preference scoring. A high benefit score cannot override an exclusion or missing essential information.

Dominant Sleep, insomnia, caffeine sensitivity or an unsafe/unknown timing window should remove caffeine from a personally recommended stack. Reference exploration may show a morning option labeled unverified.
Sliders change ranking and the set of eligible options, not unconstrained ingredient quantities. Daily reference doses and caps remain fixed.
Do not add sedating or mineral products to cancel a stimulant's unwanted effects.
interconnectedPriorityRules.status: conservative-policy; not a claim of a proven pairwise drug interaction

interconnectedPriorityRules.rule: An empty or partial stack is a valid result. Explain why an option was withheld in its existing detail/card, without adding a health-profile panel.
Do not show exact percentages of medical benefit, coverage, or personal safety from an unvalidated weighted score. Label visual scores as preference fit.
Unknown current intake is null, not zero. Never display a verified safe total or remaining daily allowance when the baseline is unknown.
